steps.title: Review site languages and Stores
steps.detail: Edit packages/site-config/localization.ts if the site needs different languages, countries or currencies. Use the same Store key for each language of a shared Store. Apply provider setup before importing localized content.

steps.title: Connect your stack
steps.detail: Create an empty stack and register its Management Token as a local csdx alias. See packages/cms-contentstack/README.md.

steps.title: Provision the content model
steps.detail: This imports the model, applies migrations, and generates GraphQL files from your stack. The bundled homepage uses /. If you use a different published path, such as /welcome, set CMS_HOMEPAGE_SLUG in the provision command’s input ENV. The command verifies that path and includes it in the web runtime settings. Pass the storefront origin with --production-url to set the runtime environment’s locale URLs. Use cms preview if the URL becomes available later or changes. Enable Live Preview and verify Visual Editor after deployment.

steps.title: Author and import site content
steps.detail: For custom content, export cms data model/schema, write an editable content folder, validate it, then run cms data setup --plan and import. Read packages/cms-core/README.md; retain the same Migrate state on retries.

steps.title: Generate GraphQL files after manual setup or model changes
steps.detail: Run before building if you set up the stack manually or changed its model after provisioning. Pass an existing runtime ENV file with the stack and Delivery Token settings. The workspace CLI provision command already generates these files.

steps.title: Configure customer access
steps.detail: Configure Clerk credentials for apps/web and its actual origin. Keep cookies host-only. See packages/auth-clerk/README.md.

steps.title: Connect customer impersonation
steps.detail: In apps/web configure customer auth credentials and the isolated ADMIN verifier. In apps/admin set IMPERSONATION_API_URL to the web HTTPS /api/auth/impersonation endpoint. Grant impersonation.read and impersonation.start to appropriate Admin operators. WorkOS additionally needs WORKOS_ENVIRONMENT_ID; enable native impersonation and configure the Initiate login URI. Native session records are the default audit source; see packages/auth-contract/impersonation.md.

steps.title: Configure administration access
steps.detail: Use a separate Clerk application for apps/admin. Configure its credentials there and matching ADMIN_CLERK_* verifier settings in each installed feature backend (apps/api for registration, apps/web for standalone impersonation or fulfillment). See packages/auth-clerk/README.md.

steps.title: Grant native shopping list access
steps.detail: Runtime credentials need view_shopping_lists and manage_shopping_lists. Grant the corresponding My/Others Shopping List permissions to Business Unit Associate Roles. Retention uses the native project shopping-list setting; configure it deliberately. See packages/commerce-core/shopping-lists/README.md.

steps.title: Configure project access
steps.detail: Provide bootstrap credentials as described in packages/commerce-commercetools/README.md.

steps.title: Deploy the optional Connect event source
steps.detail: The API receiver and event selection are already installed. Deploy a published proxy Connector that uses Connect-managed credentials. Set the same COMMERCETOOLS_WEBHOOK_SECRET in --env-file and the receiving API environment (apps/api/.env.local for local development); existing matching values need no change. Supply the full public HTTPS receiver URL with --endpoint, including /webhooks/commercetools. Connect creates the proxy's commerce credentials; no local credentials output file is needed. The command shows deployment progress and verifies the project subscription. Then publish a test product and check for HTTP 202 in API logs. See packages/commerce-commercetools/connect-proxy/README.md.
commands: pnpm --filter cli cli --env-file "$PWD/.env.bootstrap.local" commerce connect deploy --connector-key <published-proxy-key> --connector-version <published-managed-version> --deployment-key commerce-events --endpoint https://<api>/webhooks/commercetools --dry-run

steps.title: Connect the fulfillment API
steps.detail: Set FULFILLMENT_API_URL in apps/admin to the storefront HTTPS /api/commerce/fulfillment endpoint. Use a separate Admin identity application and grant fulfillment.read and fulfillment.manage to the desired operators. Each page/action and the API enforce permissions independently. See packages/commerce-core/fulfillment/README.md.

steps.title: Configure merchant access
steps.detail: Configure the selected Admin identity verifier using ADMIN_WORKOS_* or ADMIN_CLERK_* in apps/web, independently of customer credentials. The native commercetools client needs view_orders and manage_orders. To wake the optional Order workflow, configure its native Order event subscriptions (including ParcelAddedToDelivery and OrderShipmentStateChanged); installing this API does not require a workflow, email provider or Connect proxy. See packages/commerce-core/fulfillment/README.md.

steps.title: Configure order email delivery
steps.detail: This opt-in recipe installs provider-owned order processing and emails. Configure RESEND_TOKEN, a verified RESEND_FROM, COMMERCE_ORDER_ACCESS_SECRET and NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_URL in the workflow host: API for commercetools, web for Shopify. Follow the selected provider event setup and verify creation, shipping, payment terms and cancellation with a sandbox Order. Coordinate Shopify native notifications before enabling these emails. See packages/commerce-core/orders/README.md.

steps.title: Configure the API event receiver
steps.detail: Expose POST /webhooks/commercetools in the API app and configure COMMERCETOOLS_PROJECT_KEY plus COMMERCETOOLS_WEBHOOK_SECRET. A trusted relay must use the documented timestamped HMAC event protocol. Feature recipes install their consumers and native Subscription definitions; Connect deployment is optional. See packages/commerce-commercetools/webhooks/README.md.

steps.title: Connect native order events
steps.detail: Configure the API-hosted workflow. Its Order/Payment consumer and native Message types join the independent /webhooks/commercetools receiver automatically. The optional Connect recipe deploys the sender; another trusted relay can implement the signed receiver protocol. Without Connect, the native Message bearer relay at API /api/commerce/order-events remains available using COMMERCETOOLS_ORDER_EVENTS_SECRET. API runtime credentials need view_orders, manage_orders and view_payments; configure email and web Order access links there. See packages/commerce-core/orders/README.md.

steps.title: Provision the project
steps.detail: Applies starter migrations, publishes runtime credentials and revokes the bootstrap API Client.
commands:
pnpm --filter cli cli commerce project provision \
  --output commerce.env

steps.title: Connect catalog changes to the web cache
steps.detail: Set the same REVALIDATION_SECRET in API and web. On Vercel Services, bind API to web as WEB_INTERNAL_URL. Otherwise set REVALIDATION_ENDPOINT in API to the full web /api/revalidate URL. Deliver the native event subscription to API /webhooks/commercetools using a trusted signed relay. The optional Connect recipe can deploy that sender. See packages/commerce-commercetools/webhooks/README.md.

steps.title: Configure the selected custom checkout
steps.detail: This assembly installs B2C card checkout using the application-managed Checkout package. Configure the Stripe bridge and selected delivery options. Hosted Checkout is a separate B2C recipe; do not install both implementations.

steps.title: Verify the selected storefront HTTP API
steps.detail: Operations are installed at /api/commerce under the storefront origin. Check /api/commerce/openapi.json. Order endpoints require bearer authentication and an explicit allStores=true or storeKey query selection; company reads require a role granting company.orders.read in the signed app_roles claim for the selected Business Unit. This API does not require a separately deployed API application.

steps.title: Verify the selected storefront HTTP API
steps.detail: Operations are installed at /api/checkout under the storefront origin. Check /api/checkout/openapi.json. This API does not require a separately deployed API application.

steps.title: Configure Stripe credentials
steps.detail: For a Vercel demo, attach a Stripe Marketplace sandbox to the app running checkout. For other hosts, set the Stripe keys directly. Use payments provision for sandbox settings or a webhook receiver. See packages/payments-stripe/README.md.

steps.title: Verify card payments
steps.detail: Restart or redeploy the checkout app, then test checkout using Stripe sandbox credentials. See packages/payments-stripe/README.md.

steps.title: Verify a sender domain
steps.detail: Verify your sending domain in Resend. Set RESEND_FROM to an address on that domain and RESEND_TOKEN to a sending API key.

steps.title: Configure email delivery
steps.detail: Set these variables in apps/web and apps/api, restart or redeploy, and verify delivery from the application's email workflow. See packages/email/README.md.

steps.title: Create or reconcile the Algolia application and source
steps.detail: Read packages/search-algolia/docs/application-setup.md. Establish an actual Algolia Application ID, Admin key and analytics/Ingestion region before search provision. Shopify also requires Algolia AI Search & Discovery installed and synchronized in the recorded shop; the CLI does not create that installation.

steps.title: Configure Algolia access
steps.detail: Set ALGOLIA_APPLICATION_ID, ALGOLIA_ADMIN_API_KEY and ALGOLIA_REGION.

steps.title: Prepare Commerce indexing access
steps.detail: Use CTP_* management credentials with API Client, Store, Channel and Customer Group access. See packages/search-algolia/README.md for scopes and optional price audiences.

steps.title: Choose Contentstack app setup
steps.detail: Add --install-content-search-app to the command below for automatic setup; otherwise follow the manual steps in its result. Automatic setup needs the installation credentials in packages/cms-contentstack/README.md.

steps.title: Provision search
steps.detail: Use the workspace locales and a stable site-specific index prefix. Pass --locale only to select a subset. Complete the commerce source and CMS backfills, and verify actual searchable records. Index creation and credential publication alone do not complete search setup. The result lists remaining indexing and verification steps.
commands:
pnpm --filter cli cli search provision \
  --output search.env

steps.title: Connect product analytics
steps.detail: Set NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY and NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST for your project before starting the application. See packages/analytics/README.md.

steps.title: Setup notes
steps.detail: Admin is an authenticated host. Use a separate identity-provider application/project and host-only session cookies. Screen recipes contribute navigation and Admin permission definitions; each page and action must enforce its own required permissions. Registration administration uses the shared API with Admin credentials; the host alone needs no registration API URL.

steps.title: Connect error reporting
steps.detail: Set NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN to your Sentry project's DSN to enable reporting.

steps.title: Upload source maps
steps.detail: For readable stack traces, set SENTRY_ORG, SENTRY_PROJECT and SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN in the build environment. Keep the auth token server-only. See packages/observability/README.md.
